title: Finite image and local upper bounds for a coherent word prescription
statement: Fix a numerical engine R and an arbitrary simultaneous ResolutionWord-valued family ν. Let H be a finite embedded history admissible relative to ν [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history]. Assume for every history K admissible relative to ν (including every prefix and smooth restriction used in the argument) that every singular point has a ResolutionWordChart R K x [def-trf-resolution-word-charts], that ν K x equals C.word for every such chart C, and that ν K x is bottom exactly at regular points. Then the range of ν H is finite, and for every x of H.X there exists an open neighborhood U containing x with ν H y ≤ ν H x for every y in U. This result concerns one given admissible stage and does not construct ν or assert the closedness of arbitrary upper levels.

proof.text: The hypotheses used below (reduced and of finite type over $\mathbf Q$) hold at every stage of an admissible history, by induction on its length. The initial scheme of an embedded pair is reduced and of finite type, and the target of a smooth comparison is a history of another embedded pair whose centers are the extended ideals of the given ones. At a maximum extension the ambient $P_H$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], so the reduced ideal of the center $C$ is of finite type. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with center ideal $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$, the Rees algebra of [def-nagata-affine-blowup] is generated over $A$ by $a_1t,\ldots,a_rt$; hence its $\operatorname{Proj}$ is covered by the finitely many $D_+(a_it)$, whose degree-zero rings are generated by the $a_j/a_i$. Thus the glued blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] is of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, and so is its closed subscheme $X_{H+1}$. By [def-nagata-strict-transform], $X_{H+1}$ is the scheme-theoretic closure of the open part over $P_H\setminus C$, which is isomorphic to an open subscheme of the reduced $X_H$; so $X_{H+1}$ is reduced by [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image]. Use [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-smooth-dimension-profile] at the current reduced finite-type stage. Its normalized head is precisely $A_x$, with regular value $a_{\rm reg}=(1,(1,1,\ldots))$ and all singular heads strictly greater. Choose a dimension bound $D$ only for this verification. The modified head $B_D=(c,\Lambda^D\Delta^q h)$ has finite image and closed upper levels. The integer_operators assertion of the dimension-profile dependency identifies its comparisons with those of $A$, so $A$ itself has these properties. Its regular level is open: if there are singular values, exclude the closed upper level of the least of the finitely many singular heads. When there are none this open is the whole stage. Apply the simultaneous coherence hypothesis on each prefix or smooth restriction needed for the presentation argument; no property of an arbitrary unprescribed earlier value is assumed.

proof.text: Fix a finite-type stage. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian. Its underlying space is therefore a Noetherian topological space: it is a finite union of affine opens with Noetherian rings, each of which is a Noetherian space by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space], and a descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes on each of the finitely many pieces. There are finitely many heads by the dimension-profile argument. For one singular head $a$, cover its stratum $S_a$ by local presentation neighbourhoods as in the local-presentation and chart prescriptions. Each presenting marked ideal has finite word image by the engine. Their etale images are open in the stratum by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets], $S_a$ is quasi-compact even though it need not be closed in the whole stage. Choose finitely many such images; the corresponding finite union of tail images contains every value on $S_a$. Now take the finite union over the heads and include $\bot$ when it occurs. This proves finite image of $w$; it does not assume a finite cover of a non-quasi-compact arbitrary stratum.

proof.text: Here is the local upper-bound argument, which also checks the behaviour across head strata. At a singular $x$ with head $a$, first remove the closed upper level of the least occurring head strictly above $a$ (if there is one). On the resulting open neighbourhood all heads are at most $a$, so $S_a$ is closed there. A local presentation has this stratum as its cosupport, and its tail is upper semicontinuous there by the engine. Its finite image gives a relative neighbourhood of $x$ on which $t\le t(x)$: exclude the closed upper level of the least larger occurring tail, if any. If a presentation is etale-local, descend this relative open neighbourhood through its open image; independence from the assumed chart independence makes the inequality the same at all points over a fixed base point. A relative open of the closed stratum is its intersection with an ambient open. On this ambient open, points of head $a$ have tail at most $t(x)$, points of smaller singular head have strictly smaller word, and regular points have $\bot$. Hence $w\le w(x)$ near $x$. At a regular $x$ use the regular open neighbourhood of the dimension-profile argument, where $w=\bot$.

theorem resolution_word_finite_local_upper_bounds
    (R : MarkedIdeal.NumericalResolution.{u})
    (ν : ValueFamily.{u} HilbertSamuel.ResolutionWord)
    (hν : ∀ {B : EmbeddedResolutionPair.{u}} {m : ℕ}
      (K : EmbeddedResolutionHistory B m), Admissible ν K →
        (∀ x : K.X, ¬ IsRegularLocalRing (K.X.presheaf.stalk x) →
          Nonempty (ResolutionWordChart R K x)) ∧
        (∀ (x : K.X) (C : ResolutionWordChart R K x), ν K x = C.word) ∧
        (∀ x : K.X, ν K x = ⊥ ↔ IsRegularLocalRing (K.X.presheaf.stalk x)))
    {A : EmbeddedResolutionPair.{u}} {n : ℕ} (H : EmbeddedResolutionHistory A n)
    (hH : Admissible ν H) :
    (Set.range (ν H)).Finite ∧
      ∀ x : H.X, ∃ U : H.X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ ∀ y ∈ U, ν H y ≤ ν H x
